about.title: M, N, O
about.length_note: Three letters plus a quick look back at A to L fits in about 10 minutes. Pause or stop after any letter. Each letter is its own short part.

say.text: Welcome to class five. Today we meet three letters: M, N and O. There is no hurry. You can pause at any time.

First, a quick look back. Pick any letter from A to L. Say its name, then its sound. For example, A says 'a' as in apple. K says 'k' as in keys. If a letter feels hard, that is fine. We will see them all again.

show.text:
A: apple
K: keys
Your turn: pick any letter from A to L

ask.q: Which word starts with the sound for K?
ask.why: Keys begins with the 'k' sound. Apple begins with the 'a' sound.

say.text: Our first new letter is M. Its name is 'em'. Its sound is 'mmm', the sound you make when food tastes good. A familiar word is moon. A grown-up word is money.
Look at the shapes. The big M has two peaks, like two mountains. The small m has two little humps. Trace them in the air with your finger. Say 'mmm' with your lips closed.

show.text: A big capital M with two pointed peaks, and beside it a small m with two rounded humps. A finger traces each one.

ask.q: Which word starts with the 'mmm' sound?
ask.why: Moon starts with 'mmm'. Sun starts with 's', tree with 't', and door with 'd'.

say.text: Next is N. Its name is 'en'. Its sound is 'nnn', made with the tip of your tongue behind your top teeth. A familiar word is nose. A grown-up word is number.
The big N is two upright lines with a slanting line between them. The small n has just one hump. Notice that m has two humps and n has one. Trace both with your finger and say 'nnn'.

show.text:
M m: two humps, sounds 'mmm'
N n: one hump, sounds 'nnn'

ask.q: Which word starts with the 'nnn' sound?
ask.why: Nose starts with 'nnn'. Eye, hand and foot start with other sounds.

say.text: Last for today is O. Its name is 'oh'. Its common sound is a short 'o', as in orange, where the mouth opens wide. A familiar word is orange. A grown-up word is office.

O is the easiest shape of all. It is a round circle. The big O is a tall circle, and the small o is a little circle. O can also say its own name, as in 'open'. For now, start with the short sound in orange.

show.text: A big round capital O and a smaller round o, each drawn as a single smooth circle.

ask.q: Which word starts with the short 'o' sound?
ask.why: Orange starts with the short 'o' sound. Lemon, grape and pear start with other sounds.

say.text: Now let's match big and small. M goes with m. N goes with n. O goes with o. Say each pair: name, then sound, then word.

show.text:
M m: 'em', mmm, moon
N n: 'en', nnn, nose
O o: 'oh', short o, orange

ask.q: Which small letter is the partner of capital N?
ask.why: Capital N pairs with small n. Small m has two humps, and small n has one.

say.text: Well done. Today you met M, N and O. Look around you for something starting with each: moon, nose, orange, or perhaps a mug, a name or an object nearby. Next time we meet P, Q and R.
